newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares end up, haunted by political worry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares end up, haunted by political worry.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended barely higher on Monday in thin and highly selective trade, haunted by political uncertainty , brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed three points, or 0.2 percent higher at 1,470 after moving between 1,452 and 1,480. It had lost 1.7 percent last week.
Trade volume firmed to 13.43 trillion lira from Friday's 12.03 trillion.
"Support was awaited at the index's 1,450 level, so reaction buys helped the index to recover from earlier lows," said Okan Gulek from Taksim securities.

Brokers said weak turnover and caution caused activity to concentrate on three bluechip utilities for the second day in a row. The index representing these power producers and distributors posted a 3.18 percent jump.

The most heavily traded shares -- Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 187,500, Aktas Elektrik, up 10,000 lira at 190,000 and Kepez Elektrik, up 10,000 lira 252,500 -- made up 33.2 percent of the total volume.
"The market will set direction according to developments concerning the fate of the government," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.

"It will be relieved if the government falls because the coalition has not been able to take any radical decisions in the past three-four months. There has been no solid progress in vital structural reforms, particularly privatisation," he added.
Four MPs from the secularist wing of the Islamist-conservative coalition have resigned since last Tuesday when the government survived a censure motion in parliament by a close vote.

Turkish markets are awaiting the results of two meetings between top military generals and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan -- today's Supreme Military Council (YAS) and the monthly National Security Council (NSC) meeting due May 31.

The YAS meeting ended, but a statement is yet to be released. Earlier expectations were that the generals would demand that Erbakan approve the expulsion from the ranks of officers suspected of Islamist tendencies.
The NSC is expected to repeat its demands that Erbakan's government take tough measures against rising Islamist activism.

Of the 253 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 110 to 76 and 67 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN edged 0.35 percent lower to 1,412, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ leapt 2.61 percent to 1,416 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL firmed 0.19 percent to 1,614.
